issue.body:
### Issue URL (Anti Adblock Script) [https://dramadizilerim1.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdramadizilerim1.com%2F) ### Comment > **Konu: iPhone Safari – Reklam Engelleyici Algılama Uyarısı ve Sayfanın Kullanılamaması** > > Merhaba, > > iPhone cihazımda Safari tarayıcısı üzerinden **https://dramadizilerim1.com/** sitesine erişmeye çalışırken reklam engelleyici algılama sorunu yaşıyorum. > > Cihazımda AdGuard kullanıyorum. Safari koruması, DNS koruması ve gelişmiş koruma özellikleri aktif. Reklam engelleyicimi tamamen kapatmadan siteyi kullanmak istiyorum ancak site AdGuard'ı algılayarak içeriğe erişmemi engelliyor. > > **Yaşadığım sorun:** > > Siteye giriş yaptığımda ekranın ortasında "Reklam engelleyici algılandı" başlıklı bir uyarı penceresi çıkıyor. Bu pencerede reklam engelleyicimi kapatmam gerektiği belirtiliyor ve "Kapattım, devam et" butonu bulunuyor. > > Bu butona bastığımda site reklam engelleyicinin kapatılıp kapatılmadığını kontrol ediyormuş gibi davranıyor. Ancak kısa bir kontrol işleminden sonra herhangi bir değişiklik olmuyor. Aynı uyarı ekranda kalıyor ve siteye erişemiyorum. > > **Denediğim çözüm yöntemleri:** > > 1. AdGuard'ın Safari korumasının aktif olduğunu kontrol ettim. > 2. Safari uzantılarında AdGuard'a gerekli web sitesi erişim izinlerini verdim. > 3. AdGuard filtreleri arasından "Adblock Warning Removal List" filtresini etkinleştirdim. > 4. AdGuard'ın diğer rahatsız edici öğe filtrelerini kontrol ettim ve etkinleştirdim. > 5. Filtre listelerini güncelledim ve Safari'de sayfayı tekrar yükledim. > 6. Safari üzerinden AdGuard'ın manuel öğe engelleme özelliğini kullanarak uyarı penceresini gizlemeyi denedim. > 7. Bunun sonucunda uyarı penceresi görünmez oldu ancak sayfadaki hiçbir butona, bağlantıya veya başka bir öğeye tıklayamadım. > 8. Uyarı penceresinin ve onu kapsayan öğenin gizlenmesi için kullanıcı kuralları oluşturmayı denedim. > 9. Sayfadaki kaydırma ve dokunma engelini kaldırmak amacıyla özel CSS kuralı da denedim. Ancak sorun çözülmedi. > > Manuel olarak oluşturduğum kurallardan bazıları şunlardı: > > dramadizilerim1.com##div.access-screen:nth-child(4) > section.access-card > > ``` > dramadizilerim1.com##div.access-screen:nth-child(4) > ``` > > ``` > dramadizilerim1.com#$#body { overflow: auto !important; pointer-events: auto !important; } > ``` > > Bu kurallar uyarının görünürlüğünü etkileyebilse de sitenin normal şekilde kullanılmasını sağlayamadı. > > **Sorunla ilgili gözlemim:** > > Site, yalnızca bir uyarı penceresi göstermiyor olabilir. Reklam engelleyici algılandığında sayfanın diğer öğeleriyle etkileşimi de engelliyor gibi görünüyor. > > Uyarıyı manuel olarak gizlediğimde arka plandaki sayfa görüntülenebiliyor ancak kullanıcı etkileşimleri çalışmıyor. Bu nedenle yalnızca CSS ile uyarı penceresini gizlemenin yeterli olmadığını düşünüyorum. > > **Talebim:** > > AdGuard'ın bu web sitesinde reklamları engellemeye devam ederken anti-adblock algılama sisteminin oluşturduğu erişim sorununu da çözebilmesi için siteye özel bir filtre düzeltmesi yapılmasını rica ediyorum. > > Özellikle uyarı penceresinin kaldırılması, varsa sayfa üzerindeki etkileşim kilidinin giderilmesi ve sitenin reklam engelleyici açıkken normal şekilde kullanılabilmesi konusunda destek istiyorum. > > AdGuard'ın mevcut filtrelerinde bu siteye özel bir çözüm bulunuyorsa hangi ayarları veya kuralları kullanmam gerektiğini öğrenmek isterim. > > Teşekkür ederim. ### Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — stockanalysis.com shows a first-party "Stock Analysis App / Get it on Google Play / Install Now" app-install bar above the site header that no current filter hides; the proposed domain-scoped element-hiding rule removes exactly that container and was verified in the reporter's AdGuard Browser Extension profile. The report's full-screen "See Stock Analysis in..." app/browser bottom sheet did not render in the Chromium validation browser, so this rule covers the app-promotion surface that is actually present and identical in the reporter's screenshot; that Firefox-Mobile-only sheet remains uncovered. ## Rule `stockanalysis.com##div:has(> button[aria-label="Dismiss notice"]):has(> a[href^="https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.stockanalysis.app"])` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closing rules cover first-party advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls and other anti-adblock walls; none applies to a site's own mobile-app install promotion. The promoted element is the site's own app-install bar (first-party self-promotion), which the AdGuard Mobile App Banners filter is defined to block; it is not an ad served by a third party and not a paywall. No anti-adblock gate is involved:⁠ the page reports no detector, and get_applied_rules/antiAdblockDetected show no ad-recovery mechanism. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/37cd266e39a6aeac68494f161cc55671d687547a/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43345897883 Automated analysis against filters at `37cd266`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — The reported CNN subscription-offer popup ("WELCOME OFFER / Stream the CNN experience") did not appear on the article page with the reporter's filter set — a complete full-page vision pass found no modal, dimming or offer content — nor with filtering fully off, so no rule could be derived or validated. Recommend closing as not reproduced.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

The run instruction states no rule that closes this report on policy grounds:⁠ there is no anti-adblock wall (the captured network log shows no detector script, and the page shows no gate), no German anti-adblock gate, no scam/phishing page, and the article text is fully readable. Rule generation was allowed and investigated, then abandoned because the reported element never rendered:⁠ it was absent in the prepared current-extension session with the reporter's lists (complete full-page vision, reporterSymptomPresence=absent) and absent in the unfiltered control session.

issue.title: Make reporting websites easier like how it works for Easylist
issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

On Easylist github it is as easy to report a missed ad/annoyance as pasting in a screenshot and a URL.  I can report sites in less than 5 seconds after visiting this Github.  This process where I have to click like 10 buttons and drop down menus makes it take about 30-45 seconds, and discourages users from reporting sites.  I get its to have more accurate information, but it takes a toll at the cost of users reporting less.  99% of the time the annoyance is not related to the user's outdated browser extension or what not but rather the site itself, so these additional barriers I would argue don't actually offer much advantage in the big picture.

And if you are wondering why I don't just report on Easylist, well I'm banned for reporting an [annoyance on a far left winged site](https://github.com/easylist/easylist/issues/19653) that they don't want to block, as they are clearly biased.

### Proposed solution

See above

### Additional information

_No response_

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.driventic.com the reported annoyance is the site's cookie-consent panel (orestbida "Cookie Consent", root `#cc-main`, "This website uses cookies." with Manage settings / Reject all / Accept all) fixed over the hero; no current rule covers the host. The scoped candidate `driventic.com###cc-main` was verified in the reporter profile and extends the existing shared element-hiding rule for that selector in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt, hiding the panel with the page intact and no leftover instances. ## Rule `driventic.com###cc-main` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-notice/CMP annoyance; the run instruction's closing rules (first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls) do not apply, and the page shows no ad-blocker detection (apply_rule phase data:⁠ antiAdblockDetected false). The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter is documented as blocking cookie notices and CMP requests, so a rule is in scope for this filter family. The maintainer rule 'Shared rules:⁠ extend them' applies:⁠ the fix fits an existing multi-domain element-hiding rule for the same selector, so driventic.com is added to it rather than a new rule being written. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/461af7843ba88e44ed5a5db75c7db9b8a8a03fd1/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 157](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/461af7843ba88e44ed5a5db75c7db9b8a8a03fd1/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L157). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On https:⁠//bunny.net/docs the reported annoyance is the Mintlify/c15t cookie-consent banner ("We value your privacy", Reject All / Accept All / Customize) floating over the lower-left docs navigation; it was present in every baseline session. The domain-scoped element-hiding rule bunny.net#⁠#⁠[⁠data-testid="consent-banner-root"]⁠ was validated by the candidate experiment as verified (banner gone, page integrity intact, no residue), and belongs next to the existing bunny.net cookie rule in the Cookies filter. ## Rule `bunny.net##[data-testid="consent-banner-root"]` ## Policy rationale The run instruction closes only first-party advertising, paywalls and German anti-adblock walls (plus other anti-adblock walls without a captured detector script); this report is a cookie-consent notice annoyance, which none of those rules covers. The banner is the site's own consent notice rendered by its first-party Mintlify ConsentManager asset, and the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to hide exactly this kind of notice. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c815397c64c82887e3c1885c42d0bfb40730095b/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 8342](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c815397c64c82887e3c1885c42d0bfb40730095b/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L8342). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43386839941 Automated analysis against filters at `c815397`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — www⁠.edukamp.pl shows its own first-party consent dialog (orestable-style cookieconsent v3, #⁠cc--main) over the homepage hero, reproduced in both the reporter and default profiles, and the repository's shared "#⁠#⁠#⁠cc--main" family lacks this domain. Hiding it removed the dialog but every capture then reported the hero area as withheld/blank, so no candidate verified and the report needs a maintainer's judgement.

## Still visible after the rule

- Hero carousel below header/navigation / Informacje dotyczące plików cookies — Centered cookie-consent dialog headed "Informacje dotyczące plików cookies" with "Wyłącz wszystkie", "Dostosuj ⁠>" and "Zaakceptuj wszystkie" buttons is displayed over a grey dim backdrop that covers and withholds the hero carousel below the header/navigation.
- Center of the viewport, over the homepage hero carousel directly below the header/navigation — Visible cookie-consent modal headed "Informacje dotyczące plików cookies" with explanatory text and the three consent buttons "Wyłącz wszystkie", "Dostosuj ⁠>" and "Zaakceptuj wszystkie"; a grey dim backdrop covers the hero carousel and the rest of the page behind it, requiring the visitor to answer the consent notice before the page is usable.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

comment.body:
Got it. First, please check these rules.
```adb
ecosia.org##div[data-test-id^="ad-block-notice"]
ecosia.org##div[data-test-id^="ad-block-notice"] + div.notice-card__binary-feedback
```
If that doesn't help or you notice smth else, you can also check this one.
```adb
ecosia.org#%#//scriptlet('set-local-storage-item', 'adBlockNoticeDismissed', '1')
```

### Comment
> 
> Problem description
> 
> Some explicit websites with adult/NSFW content are completely accessible and are not being successfully detected or blocked by AdGuard Family DNS.
> 
> Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Configure a device to use AdGuard Family DNS (94.140.14.15 and 94.140.15.15).
> 2. Clear the browser cache and flush the local DNS cache.
> 3. Open a web browser and navigate to the unblocked adult websites.
> 4. Observe that the connection resolves successfully and the explicit content loads without being intercepted by the family filter.
> 
> Expected behavior
> 
> The domain names associated with explicit adult content should be automatically caught by the parental control filter and redirected to the standard AdGuard DNS block page.
> 
> Affected domains
> 
> • [https://xmaal.pro/]
> • [https://webxseries.vc/]

issue.title: Instagram using generated tracking parameters?

labels.name: A: In progress
labels.description: Work on the issue is in progress

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

I noticed recently that I've been seeing Instagram links from friends where there's a clear tracking parameter, but instead of the usual `igshid`, `igsh`, or `igsi` name, the parameter has some random-looking four character name. In the past couple days alone I've seen `psln`, `srtk`, and `exln`. Earlier I've also observed `stkn` and `vrfl`. The value for each is always 12-13 bytes encoded as base64.

I didn't see these parameters in the [specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/master/TrackParamFilter/sections/specific.txt) list or anyone else reporting this phenomenon, so I wanted to give a head up that they may be encoding/randomizing their tracking parameters. Given that Instagram is a huge platform (and Meta a notorious tracker), I thought you'd want to know.

### Proposed solution

This is more of a heads up than a specific feature request. The way to address this depends highly on the pattern in the parameters. It may not be worth overcomplicating the matching rules. If it's always 4 lowercase letters, though, it looks like you could use a regex to match them. If that's too broad, you can restrict it to certain paths (I've only seen these on `/reel/` urls).

### Additional information

_No response_

issue.title: Instagram using generated tracking parameters?

labels.name: A: In progress
labels.description: Work on the issue is in progress

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

I noticed recently that I've been seeing Instagram links from friends where there's a clear tracking parameter, but instead of the usual `igshid`, `igsh`, or `igsi` name, the parameter has some random-looking four character name. In the past couple days alone I've seen `psln`, `srtk`, and `exln`. Earlier I've also observed `stkn` and `vrfl`. The value for each is always 12-13 bytes encoded as base64.

I didn't see these parameters in the [specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/master/TrackParamFilter/sections/specific.txt) list or anyone else reporting this phenomenon, so I wanted to give a head up that they may be encoding/randomizing their tracking parameters. Given that Instagram is a huge platform (and Meta a notorious tracker), I thought you'd want to know.

### Proposed solution

This is more of a heads up than a specific feature request. The way to address this depends highly on the pattern in the parameters. It may not be worth overcomplicating the matching rules. If it's always 4 lowercase letters, though, it looks like you could use a regex to match them. If that's too broad, you can restrict it to certain paths (I've only seen these on `/reel/` urls).

### Additional information

_No response_

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — www⁠.performanceliebe.de serves a full-screen German cookie-consent dialog (#⁠cc-banner, "Datenschutzeinstellungen") baked into its HTML; the domain-scoped rule performanceliebe.de#⁠#⁠#⁠cc-banner was verified in the A/B/C experiment (dialog hidden, layout intact, no remaining instances) and extends the existing shared ...#⁠#⁠#⁠cc-banner rule. ## Rule `performanceliebe.de###cc-banner` ## Policy rationale The reported overlay is a cookie-consent dialog ('Datenschutzeinstellungen'), an annoyance covered by the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter; it is not first-party advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. No German anti-adblock wall clause applies:⁠ the page does not ask the visitor to disable the ad blocker; it asks for a cookie decision. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e372b74757355d2028efa3ab1045f785ab611513/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 15371](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e372b74757355d2028efa3ab1045f785ab611513/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L15371). ## Screenshots

issue.title: License question: can the URL Tracking filter's `$removeparam` rules be used under LGPL-3.0?

labels.name: A: In progress
labels.description: Work on the issue is in progress

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

I maintain [url-sanitize](https://github.com/antonio-orionus/url-sanitize), a library and CLI that removes tracking parameters from URLs (TypeScript, Rust and a Python wrapper). Its code is MIT. Its default rule catalog combines ClearURLs (LGPL-3.0) with Firefox's query-stripping list and Brave's lists (both MPL-2.0), and the native binary embeds that catalog.

We also import the `$removeparam` rules from the AdGuard URL Tracking filter (filter 17), with attribution. The filter's header points to this repository's GPL-3.0 license, so since v2.2.0 we ship those rules only in a separate opt-in package, `@url-sanitize/adguard`, labelled GPL-3.0. Putting them in the default catalog would make everything that embeds it, the CLI binary included, GPL software.

Your filter covers far more sites than the other lists we use, so most of our users never get that coverage.

### Proposed solution

Would AdGuard allow the URL Tracking filter's rules to be used under LGPL-3.0? Either of these would work for us:

1. Relicense the URL Tracking filter (or only its `$removeparam` rules) under LGPL-3.0 or a permissive license.
2. Give url-sanitize written permission to redistribute those rules under LGPL-3.0, keeping attribution to AdGuard and a link to this repository.

If the answer is no, that's fine too: the rules stay opt-in under GPL-3.0, as they are now.

### Additional information

- We fetch the compiled filter from [FiltersRegistry](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/FiltersRegistry/blob/master/filters/filter_17_TrackParam/filter.txt). That repository is LGPL-3.0, but the filter's header links to the GPL-3.0 license here, so we've followed the header. If the LGPL-3.0 already applies to the compiled filter, a short confirmation would answer this issue.
- Our import script: https://github.com/antonio-orionus/url-sanitize/blob/main/sources/adguard/sync.ts

issue.title: Make reporting websites easier like how it works for Easylist

labels.name: A: In progress
labels.description: Work on the issue is in progress

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

On Easylist github it is as easy to report a missed ad/annoyance as pasting in a screenshot and a URL.  I can report sites in less than 5 seconds after visiting this Github.  This process where I have to click like 10 buttons and drop down menus makes it take about 30-45 seconds, and discourages users from reporting sites.  I get its to have more accurate information, but it takes a toll at the cost of users reporting less.  99% of the time the annoyance is not related to the user's outdated browser extension or what not but rather the site itself, so these additional barriers I would argue don't actually offer much advantage in the big picture.

And if you are wondering why I don't just report on Easylist, well I'm banned for reporting an [annoyance on a far left winged site](https://github.com/easylist/easylist/issues/19653) that they don't want to block, as they are clearly biased.

### Proposed solution

See above

### Additional information

_No response_

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported annoyance on tangiblewp.com is the site's own first-party analytics consent bar (#⁠mk-consent / .mk-consent), a fixed full-width strip that covers the changelog text and is not covered by the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter the reporter runs. The domain-scoped element-hiding rule tangiblewp.com#⁠#⁠.mk-consent in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt verified in the CLI evidence experiment:⁠ the banner was visible on the unfiltered baseline and hidden with the candidate, no remaining instances, page integrity intact. ## Rule `tangiblewp.com##.mk-consent` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie/analytics consent notice overlay, which the repository's Cookie Notices filter (AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies) exists to hide; it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. No anti-adblock gate is involved:⁠ the page content loads fully and html/body keep overflow:⁠ visible, so a cosmetic hide is the appropriate maintainer-style fix. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/52d3568d373d21b7d7874bf11e8a01363fb2001e/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43424944225 Automated analysis against filters at `52d3568`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

### Add your comment and screenshots

Hi, I work on the YAZIO mobile apps.

The rule ||yazio-analytics.com^ from [AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters#221525](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/221525) also blocks fae.yazio-analytics.com. Our Android and iOS apps download their GrowthBook feature config from this host (/api/features/<client key>). It is a static JSON file, the same for every user, and the request sends no user data.

We use it for kill switches. If a new feature breaks, we turn it off remotely. With this rule, the app never gets the kill switch.

Could you add @@||fae.yazio-analytics.com^, or narrow the rule to the event-ingestion host?

I can send the full URL privately if you want to check it.

labels.name: A: In progress

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

On Easylist github it is as easy to report a missed ad/annoyance as pasting in a screenshot and a URL.  I can report sites in less than 5 seconds after visiting this Github.  This process where I have to click like 10 buttons and drop down menus makes it take about 30-45 seconds, and discourages users from reporting sites.  I get its to have more accurate information, but it takes a toll at the cost of users reporting less.  99% of the time the annoyance is not related to the user's outdated browser extension or what not but rather the site itself, so these additional barriers I would argue don't actually offer much advantage in the big picture.

And if you are wondering why I don't just report on Easylist, well I'm banned for reporting an [annoyance on a far left winged site](https://github.com/easylist/easylist/issues/19653) that they don't want to block, as they are clearly biased.

### Proposed solution

See above

### Additional information

_No response_

comment.body:
> I get its to have more accurate information

Indeed. This saves us from spending an hour trying to figure out the cause of the problem. Did the user turn off filtering, or was it the Basic Filter? Or broken by another ad blocker or conflict of combination?

comment.body: More info for reproducibility, and a suggested fix: 1) it is important to disable the list EasyList - Cookie Annoyances list. (which has overlapping different rules) 2) it is important to confirm that https://history.com throws up a modal dialog entitled "Legal Terms and Privacy" when adblock is disabled. (to assure that there is no "accept" cookie or other block that prevents the dialog from appearing) 3) After enabling *AdGuard - Cookie Notices*, the modal dialog is incorrectly blocked by: ``` history.com##body > div[data-sentry-element="Component"] > div:has(p > a[href="https://www.history.com/privacy-policy"]) ``` It yields a locked modal dialog that is empty: ## Suggestion In order to fully block the modal dialog, and allow scrolling thereafter, I recommend removing the existing history.com rule above, and also the proposed history.com css rule, and instead using the following (the first two are taken from EasyList - Cookie Annoyances, and the third is the additional rule to prevent scrolling from being disabled): ``` ! history.com: block modal dialog, base overlay, and useEffect() that prevents scrolling history.com##[data-sentry-component="Box"]:has-text(Legal Terms and Privacy) history.com##.p11s5o4 history.com##+js(set-constant, document.body.style.overflow, "") ```

issue.title: License question: can the URL Tracking filter's `$removeparam` rules be used under LGPL-3.0?

labels.name: A: In progress
labels.description: Work on the issue is in progress

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

I maintain [url-sanitize](https://github.com/antonio-orionus/url-sanitize), a library and CLI that removes tracking parameters from URLs (TypeScript, Rust and a Python wrapper). Its code is MIT. Its default rule catalog combines ClearURLs (LGPL-3.0) with Firefox's query-stripping list and Brave's lists (both MPL-2.0), and the native binary embeds that catalog.

We also import the `$removeparam` rules from the AdGuard URL Tracking filter (filter 17), with attribution. The filter's header points to this repository's GPL-3.0 license, so since v2.2.0 we ship those rules only in a separate opt-in package, `@url-sanitize/adguard`, labelled GPL-3.0. Putting them in the default catalog would make everything that embeds it, the CLI binary included, GPL software.

Your filter covers far more sites than the other lists we use, so most of our users never get that coverage.

### Proposed solution

Would AdGuard allow the URL Tracking filter's rules to be used under LGPL-3.0? Either of these would work for us:

1. Relicense the URL Tracking filter (or only its `$removeparam` rules) under LGPL-3.0 or a permissive license.
2. Give url-sanitize written permission to redistribute those rules under LGPL-3.0, keeping attribution to AdGuard and a link to this repository.

If the answer is no, that's fine too: the rules stay opt-in under GPL-3.0, as they are now.

### Additional information

- We fetch the compiled filter from [FiltersRegistry](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/FiltersRegistry/blob/master/filters/filter_17_TrackParam/filter.txt). That repository is LGPL-3.0, but the filter's header links to the GPL-3.0 license here, so we've followed the header. If the LGPL-3.0 already applies to the compiled filter, a short confirmation would answer this issue.
- Our import script: https://github.com/antonio-orionus/url-sanitize/blob/main/sources/adguard/sync.ts

comment.body:
Thanks for looking at this. The filter's header says GPL-3.0, and GPL-3.0 has a "copyleft" rule. If we put your rules into our default rule catalog, anything that ships that catalog would have to be released under GPL-3.0 too. That includes our CLI binary and every app that bundles our library. Most of those apps are MIT or closed source, so they couldn't use the library anymore.

That's why your rules are now in a separate opt-in package, and most users never install it.

We don't need you to change anything in the filter itself. A short statement here would be enough, for example:

> url-sanitize may include the `$removeparam` rules from the AdGuard URL Tracking filter in its default catalog under LGPL-3.0, with attribution to AdGuard and a link to this repository.

If AdGuard prefers to keep the rules GPL-only, that's fine. We'll keep them opt-in as they are now.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On mangaraw.org.uk a page click opens an ad pop-under to a randomized adsgateway.net URL; the ad document is already blocked by ||adsgateway.net^$document, but the pop-up window still opens, matching the report. A scriptlet candidate, mangaraw.*#⁠%#⁠//scriptlet('prevent-window-open'), cut the per-phase pop-up count from 1 (baseline) to 0 (candidate) with the page intact, but the vision review could only judge it inconclusive, so the exact rule goes to human review.

## Candidate for review

`mangaraw.*#%#//scriptlet('prevent-window-open')`

AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt

Not verified: Not verified:⁠ the third apply_rule run returned environmentExperiment='inconclusive' and visualReview verdict 'inconclusive' (symptom unclear, adLayoutResidue absent, remainingInstances [⁠]⁠, pageIntegrity intact, observedDamage [⁠]⁠), because a click-triggered pop-up cannot be shown in static before/after frames. The behavioural proof is the per-phase revealSteps counts with the same steps completed in every phase (identical=true):⁠ phase A popupsOpened=1, phase B (baseline lists) popupsOpened=1, phase C (candidate) popupsOpened=0. The two earlier runs (card click) reported the symptom resolved with no ad-layout residue but were rejected only for page-owned artefacts on the pages reached:⁠ unloaded lazy cover images (61 of 88 homepage covers stay unloaded with loading='lazy' in this environment regardless of any rule) and the site's sticky bottom nav, neither of which a prevent-window-open scriptlet can influence.

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — www⁠.silverfriend.de (AdGuard Mini for Mac report, comment "cookie") shows a first-party German cookie-consent card fixed at the bottom of the viewport, which the prepared extension baseline does not hide. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule for that fixed bottom container was verified in the browser:⁠ the card is hidden, nothing else on the page is affected, and no residue or scroll problem appears. ## Rule `silverfriend.de##div.fixed.inset-x-0.bottom-0.z-50.animate-slide-up` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported symptom is a cookie-consent notice, not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall that detects a blocker and asks to disable it; the German anti-adblock close rule therefore does not apply. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter policy explicitly covers cookie notices, preferring to hide them when the site works without a consent decision, which the live page does (no dim overlay, no scroll lock, page content and scrolling intact). The notice is baked into the first-party Next.js page bundle with no third-party vendor loader in the captured requests, so no maintainer hand-off criterion for an uncorroborated anti-adblock detector applies. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ad73e42576d8a31b259350e6e11081b800fe7724/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On djpunjab2.in (a DexDrop APK download page) the baseline lists block the al5sm.com ad-tag script and redirect GPT, leaving empty ad containers:⁠ two blank bands around the header, an empty "SPONSORED ANNOUNCEMENT" overlay with only a CLOSE button, and reserved blank GPT gaps inside the download panel. One domain-scoped element-hiding rule was validated by apply_rule:⁠ all 19 ad-container matches go to zero area, document height drops 1488→1080px, page integrity stays intact. ## Rule `djpunjab2.in##.ad-container, #stickyTopAd, #stickyBottomAd, .ad-popup-overlay, .dj-gpt-wrap, div:has(> .dj-gpt-wrap)` ## Policy rationale The issue is an ad-blocking report (empty leftover ad containers), not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall and not a scam/phishing page, so none of the run instruction's close rules applies. The leftover containers carry third-party ad slots (Google Ad Manager slots filled via securepubads.g.doubleclick.net and the al5sm.com ad tag), not the site's own self-promotion, so this is not the 'site's own advertising' case. The rule restores what the published lists already intended by hiding only the emptied ad containers; it needs no anti-adblock request evidence because the reported symptom is not an anti-adblock wall (the page's #⁠adblockModal stayed display:⁠none in every phase). ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ad73e42576d8a31b259350e6e11081b800fe7724/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"23453e484fea7b52d89968dc99e383c35c316182c2471703f58203048512a40a"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

On tarnkappe.info the filtered page still renders the whole advertorial (featured image, headline, lead, body, TOC); what makes "the article not show" is the site's own German ad-blocker wall ("Kein Bock auf Werbung? … Dieser Hinweis erscheint, weil du einen Werbeblocker verwendest. Die Tarnkappe lässt sich nur ohne Werbeblocker lesen." plus "Anleitung zum Deaktivieren"). The run instruction's filter policy puts German anti-adblock walls out of scope, so no rule is proposed and closing is recommended for a maintainer to decide.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "German anti-adblock walls:⁠ no rule; recommend closing. This covers only a German site's wall or popup that detects the ad blocker and asks to disable it or to allowlist the site." The page itself shows the wall:⁠ "Dieser Hinweis erscheint, weil du einen Werbeblocker verwendest. Die Tarnkappe lässt sich nur ohne Werbeblocker lesen." with an "Anleitung zum Deaktivieren" link to instructions for disabling the ad blocker — a German-language site detecting the ad blocker and asking to disable it. The wall is injected only when filtering is active:⁠ #⁠anti-adblock-modal exists in the reporter-profile session and is absent in the unfiltered control session on the same URL. No repository rule removes the article:⁠ the article body and featured image are present and laid out with the reporter's lists; the circled empty band is an emptied site ad slot, and the site's own advertising must not be deliberately unblocked. The agent does not close issues; the report recommends closing and a maintainer decides.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43458192582

<sub>Automated analysis against filters at `152cc67`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.</sub>

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The businesstimes.com.sg article renders a Google "Add to Preferred Sources" prompt pill in the article toolbar — the element the reporter's arrow points at — and no existing rule hides it. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule on button[⁠data-testid="article-google-prefered-source-button"]⁠ was verified in the locked CLI baseline:⁠ the pill is visible before and gone after, with the page intact and no layout residue. ## Rule `businesstimes.com.sg##button[data-testid="article-google-prefered-source-button"]` ## Policy rationale The reported element is a Google 'Add to Preferred Sources' prompt, an in-page annoyance widget, not the site's own advertising, a paywall, or an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's close rules applies. It is also not a scam/phishing/tech-support page case; it is handled as an ordinary annoyance-element report. Maintainer guidance is followed:⁠ the fix fits the repository's existing Google-preferred-sources rule family in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt, but that shared rule targets an <⁠a href^="https:⁠//google.com/preferences/source?q="⁠> while this site renders a <⁠button data-testid=...⁠>, so domain extension alone cannot cover it and a site rule is required. Placement follows the contributing guide:⁠ businesstimes.com.sg already has a rules group in that same file (newsletter widget rules at lines 2645-2646), so the new rule joins the site's group. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/64bd3edc3bf4c85004f6773f1cf4568f669d4b93/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On myradioonline.pl/rmf-fm the site's own "Tekst piosenki" dialog (the same dialog that shows the Polish anti-adblock message in the reporter's screenshot) is hidden by the over-broad repository rule myradioonline.pl#⁠#⁠.popup_layer:⁠ the unfiltered phase shows it filled with lyrics, the filtered baseline shows nothing. Narrowing the rule restored the dialog in the experiment, but the vision review rejected the candidate because the player's album-cover slot and the related-news block stay empty — both are equally empty without filtering — and the reporter's detected-adblock path cannot fire on this egress.

## Missing information

- Baseline omits the reporter's AdGuard Polish filter, so its rules could not be tested: The locked adguard_cli baseline reports skippedSources:⁠ {"kind":⁠"unresolved_name","reportedName":⁠"AdGuard Polish"} (and "EasyList Lithuania", third_party_catalog). The reporter's settings list AdGuard Polish as enabled, and this repository keeps myradioonline.pl rules in PolishFilter/sections/specific.txt, so any Polish-filter rule involved in the reported incorrect blocking could neither be applied nor identified in this run. Also missing:⁠ the reporter's DNS-level AdGuard DNS filter and the beta AdGuard Extra / Popup Blocker userscripts are not part of the verification environment, and this egress receives no ad configuration from the site (no adsense/publisher requests, AddAdsV2I.hasAdblock() stays false), so the site's ad-block detection path shown in the reporter's screenshot cannot be triggered here.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — kabanychrr4.com shows a full-screen Russian anti-adblock dialog that also locks page scrolling; hiding only the dialog left the page unscrollable, so a single domain-scoped CSS injection rule that pushes the gate off-screen and restores html/body overflow was verified in the reporter-settings extension session (symptom resolved, page integrity intact). ## Rule `kabanychrr4.com#$#html[class].rr4-support-guard-open, body[class].rr4-support-guard-open, #rr4-site-support-guard { overflow: visible !important; top: 100000px !important; }` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The wall is Russian-language, not a German site, so the German anti-adblock closure does not apply. The page's captured requests show the first-party detector/UI script (`/site-support-guard.js?v=20261025guard3`, artifact:⁠har:⁠7fe0aa77-c9f8-4c79-8019-b7c4bc0da936), satisfying the requirement for other anti-adblock walls. The wall overlays the whole viewport and disables scrolling, i.e. it effectively prevents using the website, which the filter policy lists as a case where anti-adblock walls are blocked. ## Place in the list [CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/152cc67343879a0c7f0a04f5ed252f3407b34e8d/CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
